# DailymotionVideo

Video component that plays Dailymotion videos through a Dailymotion player configuration

The Dailymotion player plays videos inside a player configuration you create in [Dailymotion Studio](https://www.dailymotion.com/partner/embed/players), and this component drives it through the [Dailymotion Web SDK](https://developers.dailymotion.com/reference/web-sdk-player-methods). Dailymotion refuses any embed that doesn’t name a player configuration, so every source carries a Player ID. See [Create a Player](https://developers.dailymotion.com/docs/create-a-player) in the official Dailymotion documentation.

> **Caution: Works without a skin**
>
> Dailymotion’s terms don’t allow covering its player, so this component uses Dailymotion’s own controls instead of a Video.js skin (see [Use Dailymotion’s controls](#use-dailymotions-controls)). If you need it to work with a skin, [open an issue](https://github.com/videojs/video.js/issues) describing your use case.

## Import

```bash
pnpm add @videojs/dailymotion-video
```

```tsx
import { DailymotionVideo } from '@videojs/react/media/dailymotion-video';
```

## Load a source

The simplest `src` is the player embed URL Dailymotion Studio gives you, which names both the player configuration and the video:

```tsx
<DailymotionVideo src="https://geo.dailymotion.com/player/x8lr5.html?video=x84sh87" />
```

### Specify the Player ID

These URLs name a video but no player configuration, so pair them with `engine.dailymotion.player`:

- Video page URLs: `dailymotion.com/video/<id>`
- Legacy embed URLs: `dailymotion.com/embed/video/<id>`, or `geo.dailymotion.com/player.html?video=<id>`, where they now redirect
- Short links: `dai.ly/<id>`

`engine.dailymotion.player` also wins over the configuration a player embed URL names. [Configure the player in Dailymotion Studio](#configure-the-player-in-dailymotion-studio) covers where a Player ID comes from. Dailymotion’s [runtime parameters](https://developers.dailymotion.com/reference/web-sdk-player-runtime-parameters) go next to it:

```tsx
<DailymotionVideo
  source={{
    src: 'https://www.dailymotion.com/video/x84sh87',
    engine: { dailymotion: { player: 'x8lr5', startTime: 10 } },
  }}
/>
```

The URL’s query can also carry Dailymotion’s `startTime` (or the older `start`), `scaleMode`, and `customConfig[key]=value`, as Dailymotion’s iframe embed reads them; `engine.dailymotion` wins over them. `loop`, `autoplay`, and mute come from the component’s own props.

Without a Player ID, the component reports a `MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED` error instead of creating a player Dailymotion would reject, and in development it logs a warning that points to `engine.dailymotion.player`. The SDK script is loaded from `geo.dailymotion.com` with the first player created on the page; under a [Content Security Policy](../../guides/content-security-policy.md), allow that origin.

## Use Dailymotion’s controls

Dailymotion’s [Terms of Use](https://legal.dailymotion.com/en/terms-of-use/) don’t allow blocking any part of its embedded player, including its links back to Dailymotion. So the component always lets the player take pointer input, and Dailymotion’s own controls, logo, and links stay usable.

A [skin](../../guides/skins.md) doesn’t work over the player, which takes the pointer input over the video before the skin can see it, so use the component without one, as in [Basic Usage](#basic-usage).

## Configure the player in Dailymotion Studio

Create a player configuration on the Players page in [Dailymotion Studio](https://www.dailymotion.com/partner/embed/players). Its Player ID is the part of the player embed URL Studio gives you after `/player/`: `x8lr5` in `geo.dailymotion.com/player/x8lr5.html`.

The player configuration decides what the embed can’t change at runtime:

| Setting | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Controls | Which of Dailymotion’s controls show. `controls` has no effect. |
| Autostart | `autoplay` decides whether the video starts: with it off, the component pauses the configuration’s autostart as it starts. An ad that plays first is never paused, and the video after it is. Turning Autostart off avoids the pause. |
| Autonext | When the player moves on to the next video by itself, `src` still names the one you loaded. It also overrides `loop`: the video stops at the end, and the component reports `ended`. |
| Picture-in-picture | Dailymotion’s picture-in-picture moves the player out of the element. |
| Poster, preload, and inline playback | `poster`, `preload`, and `playsinline` are accepted for parity with `<video>` but have no effect. |

## Behavior

- Volume and mute both work, like a native `<video>`. Dailymotion has no separate mute, so muting sets its volume to `0` and unmuting restores the previous level.
- `playbackRate` takes Dailymotion’s rates, `0.25` to `2` in steps of `0.25`. Dailymotion rounds any other value up to the next one and caps it at `2`, and `playbackRate` then reports the rate it plays at.
- `loop` is passed to Dailymotion, which restarts the video itself.
- A new source loads into the same player while the Player ID and the runtime parameters other than `startTime` stay the same, whether they come from `engine.dailymotion` or the URL’s query. Any other change creates a new player, since Dailymotion only reads them when a player is created. So does `autoplay`, but only at the next load: call `load()` to apply a change right away. `muted` and `loop` change in place.
- Depending on the player configuration, Dailymotion may ignore a seek made before the video first plays, and playback then starts from the beginning. To start at a known position, set `startTime` on the source (under `engine.dailymotion`, or in the URL) instead: Dailymotion applies it on load.
- Seeking while paused stays paused, as on a native `<video>`. Dailymotion starts playback on a seek from its start or end screen, and the component pauses it again as it starts, unless an ad plays first.
- The SDK reports no buffered range, so `buffered` ends at the furthest point played.
- Ads play inside the embed, and the component never pauses one. `paused` follows the ad while it plays, but `currentTime` and `duration` always describe the video.
- When the browser refuses to start playback, as it does for unmuted autoplay, the component reports `pause` instead of playing.
- Fullscreen targets the element the player is built in.

## Examples

### Basic Usage

**App.tsx**

```tsx
import { DailymotionVideo } from '@videojs/react/media/dailymotion-video';

export default function BasicUsage() {
  return (
    <div className="dailymotion-video">
      <DailymotionVideo muted src="https://geo.dailymotion.com/player/x8lr5.html?video=x84sh87" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

**App.css**

```css
.dailymotion-video {
  width: 100%;
  aspect-ratio: 16 / 9;
}
```

## API Reference

### Props

Accepts these Video.js-specific props:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `autoplay` | `boolean` | `false` | Starts playback on each load, through Dailymotion's `autoplay` parameter and a play sent once the player is ready. When off, a player configuration whose Autostart is on is paused as it starts, unless an ad plays first. |
| `controls` | `boolean` | `false` | Has no effect: the player configuration decides whether Dailymotion's controls show, which the SDK can't change. |
| `defaultMuted` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `loop` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `muted` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `playsInline` | `boolean` | `true` | |
| `poster` | `string` | `''` | |
| `preload` | `MediaPreloadType` | `'metadata'` | |
| `source` | `{ src?: string; engine?: DailymotionSourceEngineConfig } \| null` | `null` | Dailymotion video URL in `src`, player configuration and parameters under `engine.dailymotion`. |
| `src` | `string` | `''` | |

### Engine options

#### `source.engine.dailymotion`

Pass the Player ID as `player`, plus [Dailymotion runtime parameters](https://developers.dailymotion.com/reference/web-sdk-player-runtime-parameters) under `source.engine.dailymotion`, spelled exactly as Dailymotion spells them. [Media Sources](../../guides/media-sources.md) covers how engine options fit into a structured source.

The video comes from `src`, and `loop` and `autoplay` from the props of the same name, so none of them has an `engine.dailymotion` spelling. Mute isn’t a runtime parameter either: the component applies it through the SDK. [Configure the player in Dailymotion Studio](#configure-the-player-in-dailymotion-studio) lists what only the player configuration decides, such as controls.

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `customConfig` | `Record<string, string> \| undefined` | Advertising key-values ([https://developers.dailymotion.com/docs/custom-config](https://developers.dailymotion.com/docs/custom-config)). |
| `player` | `string \| undefined` | Player ID of a player configuration from Dailymotion Studio. Required unless `src` is a player embed URL, which names its own; this one wins over it. |
| `referrerPolicy` | `ReferrerPolicy \| undefined` | `referrerpolicy` for the iframe the SDK builds. |
| `scaleMode` | `'fit' \| 'fill' \| 'fillLeft' \| 'fillRight' \| 'fillTop' \| 'fillBottom' \| undefined` | How the video fills the player. Defaults to `'fit'`. |
| `startTime` | `number \| undefined` | Start position in seconds. |

### Refs

#### `ref`

Forwards to the rendered `<div>`, an [HTMLDivElement](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLDivElement). The `<div>` cannot play or seek; use [`mediaRef`](#mediaref) for playback.

```tsx
const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

<DailymotionVideo ref={ref} />
```

#### `mediaRef`

Receives the `DailymotionAdapter` that drives the embed, which exposes media methods and properties such as `play()` and `currentTime`. It is set once the adapter has attached to the `<div>`, so its `target` is already that element, and it is cleared when the element unmounts.

```tsx
import type { DailymotionAdapter } from '@videojs/dailymotion-video';

const mediaRef = useRef<DailymotionAdapter>(null);

<DailymotionVideo mediaRef={mediaRef} />

// In an event handler
mediaRef.current?.play();
```

### Events

Handle standard media events with React event props such as `onPlay` and `onTimeUpdate`. The adapter dispatches them, not the `<div>`. For events without a React prop, call `addEventListener` on the adapter from `mediaRef`.
